turns.response_html:
Hello! It is great to help you with this. Since you are a software engineer, we can definitely have some fun with the "Google Cloud Platform scripts" (specifically Google Apps Script, which is likely what you want for internal Gmail automation) to build a robust system.

Given that you are juggling contract work, a Master’s program at ISU, and complex hobbies like electronics and beekeeping, a standard folder system often fails because a single email (e.g., a receipt for a Raspberry Pi) might fit into "Finances," "Projects," and "Hobbies."

Here is a strategy to "start over" and organize your Gmail, moving from native features to custom scripting.

Phase 1: The "Life-Stream" Taxonomy (Starting Over)

Since you mentioned your current folders aren't intuitive, I recommend flattening your hierarchy into Streams (Areas of Responsibility) rather than just "Topics."

Delete your old labels (the emails won't be deleted, just the tags) and create these high-level parent labels based on what we know about your activities:

  • 0_Inbox (For high-priority routing)
  • 1_Work
    • Neapolitan Labs (Contract)
    • Fareway
    • Admin/Tax
  • 2_School (ISU M.A.T)
    • Coursework
    • Admin
  • 3_Service
    • VA Benefits
    • Healthcare
  • 4_Maker_Space (Your Projects)
    • Electronics/Robotics
    • Beekeeping
    • Supplies/Receipts (Adafruit, eBay)
  • 5_Read_Later
    • Newsletters
    • Job Alerts

Why the numbers? Gmail sorts labels alphabetically. Prefixing with numbers forces your most critical categories to the top of the sidebar.

Phase 2: Native Gmail Power Tools (No Code Needed)

Before writing scripts, use Gmail’s native "Multiple Inboxes" feature. This is often more powerful than scripts for visual organization.

  1. Turn on Multiple Inboxes: Go to Settings > Inbox > Inbox type: Multiple Inboxes.
  2. Configure Sections:
    • Pane 1: label:1_work OR label:2_school (Keeps your contract and grad school work front and center).
    • Pane 2: is:starred (For immediate to-dos).
    • Pane 3: label:5_read_later (So these don't clog your main view).

The "Archive" Rule: If an email does not require action today, it should be labeled and archived immediately. Your "Inbox" should only contain unread or urgent items.

Phase 3: Google Apps Script Automation

Since native filters are limited (they can't do complex date math or regex on the body), we can use Google Apps Script.

To access this: Go to drive.google.com > New > More > Google Apps Script.

Script 1: The "Stale Content" Purge

You likely receive recurring notifications (like Job Alerts for "Software Engineer" or shipping updates) that are useless after 30 days. This script cleans them up automatically.

function cleanUpOldEmails() {
  // Config: Label name and age in days
  var rules = [
    {label: "5_Read_Later/Job Alerts", days: 14},
    {label: "Promotions", days: 30},
    {label: "Updates", days: 60}
  ];

  rules.forEach(function(rule) {
    var delay = rule.days;
    var maxDate = new Date();
    maxDate.setDate(maxDate.getDate() - delay);
    
    // Format date for Gmail search query (YYYY/MM/DD)
    var dateString = Utilities.formatDate(maxDate, Session.getScriptTimeZone(), "yyyy/MM/dd");
    
    // Search for emails older than X days in this label
    var query = "label:" + rule.label + " before:" + dateString;
    
    var threads = GmailApp.search(query, 0, 100); // Batch size 100 to avoid timeouts
    
    if (threads.length > 0) {
      GmailApp.moveThreadsToTrash(threads); // Or use archiveThreads(threads) to just remove from inbox
      Logger.log("Moved " + threads.length + " threads to trash from " + rule.label);
    }
  });
}

Script 2: The "Project Router" (Regex Labeling)

Native Gmail filters struggle with complex "OR" logic inside email bodies. This script scans your inbox for keywords related to your specific projects (like specific chips or beekeeping terms) and labels them, even if the subject line is vague.

function autoLabelProjects() {
  var threads = GmailApp.getInboxThreads(0, 50); // Process last 50 inbox threads
  
  // Define your keywords
  var electronicsKeywords = /raspberry pi|pico|l515|soldering|adafruit/i;
  var beeKeywords = /hive|queen|honey|colony|swarm/i;
  var schoolKeywords = /canvas|syllabus|assignment|grade/i;

  var labelElec = GmailApp.getUserLabelByName("4_Maker_Space/Electronics/Robotics");
  var labelBee = GmailApp.getUserLabelByName("4_Maker_Space/Beekeeping");
  var labelSchool = GmailApp.getUserLabelByName("2_School/Coursework");

  threads.forEach(function(thread) {
    var messages = thread.getMessages();
    var body = messages[0].getPlainBody(); // Check the first message content
    var subject = messages[0].getSubject();
    var content = subject + " " + body;

    if (electronicsKeywords.test(content)) {
      thread.addLabel(labelElec);
    }
    if (beeKeywords.test(content)) {
      thread.addLabel(labelBee);
    }
    if (schoolKeywords.test(content)) {
      thread.addLabel(labelSchool);
    }
  });
}

To automate these: inside the Apps Script editor, click on the "Triggers" (clock icon) on the left. Set cleanUpOldEmails to run Daily and autoLabelProjects to run Hourly.

Phase 4: Implementation Plan

  1. The Wipe: Create your new labels (0-5 structure above). Do not delete your old folders yet; just rename them to z_Old/[FolderName] so they drop to the bottom of your list.
  2. The Filters: Create standard Gmail filters for your "Big Rocks":
    • from:*@neapolitanlabs.com -> Apply Label 1_Work/Neapolitan.
    • from:*@iastate.edu -> Apply Label 2_School.
    • from:*@va.gov -> Apply Label 3_Service/VA Benefits.
  3. The Scripts: Deploy the "Stale Content" script first. It is the safest way to instantly reduce clutter by removing outdated notifications.

Would you like me to generate a specific list of keywords for the scripts based on your recent project purchases (like the specific sensor names or tools)?

Because you are a developer, I have written a setup script to instantly create this exact hierarchy for you (so you don't have to click "Create new label" 12 times), followed by the logic script to sort your mail into them.

Step 1: The "Architect" Script

Copy this into your Google Apps Script project. It will ensure all your folders exist with the correct nesting.

function createLabelHierarchy() {
  // The structure you defined
  const labelsToCreate = [
    "Finances",
    "Finances/CreditCards",
    "Finances/Hobbies",

Step 2: The "Sorter" Script

This script uses regex matching to route emails. I have pre-filled it with the domain logic based on your profile (ISU, Fareway, Neapolitan Labs).

function autoOrganizeInbox() {
  // Process the last 50 threads in the Inbox
  var threads = GmailApp.getInboxThreads(0, 50);
  
  // --- RULES CONFIGURATION ---
  // Format: { label: "Label/Name", check: function(text, sender) }
  var rules = [
    {
      label: "Work/NeopolitanLabs",
      regex: /@neapolitanlabs\.com/i // Matches sender domain
    },
    {
      label: "Work/Fareway",
      regex: /fareway|schedule|shift/i 
    },
    {
      label: "Work/Linkedin",
      regex: /linkedin\.com|invitation to connect/i
    },
    {
      label: "School/Iowa State",
      regex: /@iastate\.edu|canvas|syllabus/i
    },
    {
      label: "School/Georgia Tech",
      regex: /@gatech\.edu|omscs/i
    },
    {
      label: "School/Ankeny High School",
      regex: /ankeny\.k12\.ia\.us|student teaching|cooperating teacher/i
    },
    {
      label: "Finances/BeeKeeping",
      regex: /hive|queen bee|swarm|mann lake/i
    },
    {
      label: "Finances/Hobbies",
      // Catch-all for electronics/making if not beekeeping
      regex: /raspberry pi|arduino|soldering|adafruit|lego/i
    }
  ];

  // --- EXECUTION LOOP ---
  threads.forEach(function(thread) {
    var messages = thread.getMessages();
    var firstMsg = messages[0];
    var sender = firstMsg.getFrom();
    var subject = firstMsg.getSubject();
    var body = firstMsg.getPlainBody().substring(0, 500); // Check first 500 chars for speed
    var fullText = sender + " " + subject + " " + body;

    rules.forEach(function(rule) {

        var label = GmailApp.getUserLabelByName(rule.label);

Important Nuance on "BeeKeeping"

In your list, you placed BeeKeeping under Finances.

  • If you intended this: The script above works perfectly. It will put receipt emails and general bee chat into Finances/BeeKeeping.
  • If you made a mistake: If you want BeeKeeping to be its own top-level hobby category (not just for money), just change the string in the script to "BeeKeeping" (or "Hobbies/BeeKeeping") and run the createLabelHierarchy function again.

Handling the "Missing" Items

Your new list is very clean, but it leaves out a few things we discussed earlier. I recommend creating standard Gmail filters (Settings > Filters) for these "Utility" items so they don't clog your main script:

  1. VA / Military Benefits: Filter from:va.gov $\rightarrow$ Label Finances (or create a Service label if you prefer).
  2. Apartment Hunting: Since you are looking in Ames, filter subject:"lease" OR subject:"tour" $\rightarrow$ Label Finances (or Work/Contractual if it relates to relocation).

Since you have given the green light to re-architect and make this a larger project, we are going to treat your Gmail account less like a mailbox and more like a relational database.

As a software engineer, you know the limitation of your previous list: Single Inheritance. You put Beekeeping under Finances, which means a non-financial email about a "swarm alert" has nowhere to go.

We will switch to a Poly-Hierarchical System (Tagging). We will write a script that can apply multiple labels to a single thread. A receipt for a new Hive Tool will be tagged 40_Projects/Beekeeping AND 90_Finances/Receipts.

Here is the Version 2.0 Architecture.

1. The Schema (The 10-90 System)

We will use numbered prefixes. This forces the sorting order in the UI and creates "buckets" for your brain.

  • 00_Inbox_Triage (Optional: Automated "Urgent" flagging)
  • 10_Work
    • 11_Neapolitan
    • 12_Fareway
    • 13_Contractual
    • 14_Job_Hunt (LinkedIn, Alerts)
  • 20_Academia
    • 21_ISU_Masters (Current)
    • 22_Ankeny_Teaching (Student Teaching/Fieldwork)
    • 23_GT_Archive (OMSCS records)
  • 30_Projects (The "Doing")
    • 31_Beekeeping (Husbandry, logs, chats)
    • 32_Electronics (Raspberry Pi, Code, Soldering)
    • 33_Home_Lab (Servers, Network)
  • 40_Logistics (The "Living")
    • 41_Housing (Ames apartment hunt, Lease docs)
    • 42_Medical_VA (Benefits, Appts)
    • 43_Vehicle
  • 90_Finances (The "Money")
    • 91_Receipts (The catch-all for anything purchased)
    • 92_Banks_Credit
    • 93_Tax_Docs

2. The Engine (Google Apps Script)

We are going to write a class-based script. This allows you to easily scale it later.

Create a new script file called Main.gs and paste this:

// --- CONFIGURATION ---
const RULES = [
  // WORK & CAREER
  { regex: /@neapolitanlabs\.com/i, labels: ["10_Work/11_Neapolitan"] },
  { regex: /fareway|produce.*report|store.*manager/i, labels: ["10_Work/12_Fareway"] },
  { regex: /linkedin|apply|application|recruiter/i, labels: ["10_Work/14_Job_Hunt"] },

  // ACADEMIA
  { regex: /@iastate\.edu|canvas|syllabus|praxis/i, labels: ["20_Academia/21_ISU_Masters"] },
  { regex: /ankeny\.k12\.ia\.us|cooperating teacher/i, labels: ["20_Academia/22_Ankeny_Teaching"] },

  // PROJECTS (The Fun Stuff)
  { regex: /hive|queen|colony|apiary|mann lake/i, labels: ["30_Projects/31_Beekeeping"] },
  { regex: /raspberry pi|arduino|pico|adafruit|esp32|github/i, labels: ["30_Projects/32_Electronics"] },

  // LOGISTICS
  { regex: /lease|rent|deposit|ames.*apartments/i, labels: ["40_Logistics/41_Housing"] },
  { regex: /va\.gov|tricare|veteran/i, labels: ["40_Logistics/42_Medical_VA"] },

  // FINANCES (The "Cross-Cutting" Concern)
  { 
    regex: /order confirmed|receipt|invoice|payment processed|transaction/i, 
    labels: ["90_Finances/91_Receipts"] 
  },
  { regex: /statement|balance|payment due|american express|visa/i, labels: ["90_Finances/92_Banks_Credit"] }
];

// --- MAIN FUNCTION ---
function runInboxProcessor() {
  const processor = new GmailProcessor();
  processor.ensureLabelsExist(); // Self-healing: creates folders if missing
  processor.processInbox();
}

// --- CLASS DEFINITION ---
class GmailProcessor {
  constructor() {
    this.batchSize = 50; // Gmail limit is tight, keep it small and run often
  }

  // 1. ARCHITECTURE BUILDER
  ensureLabelsExist() {
    const allLabels = new Set();
    RULES.forEach(r => r.labels.forEach(l => allLabels.add(l)));
    
    allLabels.forEach(labelPath => {
      try {
        GmailApp.createLabel(labelPath);
      } catch (e) {
        // Label likely exists, ignore
      }
    });
  }

  // 2. THE SORTING HAT
  processInbox() {
    const threads = GmailApp.getInboxThreads(0, this.batchSize);
    
    threads.forEach(thread => {
      const messages = thread.getMessages();
      const firstMsg = messages[0];
      const content = `${firstMsg.getFrom()} ${firstMsg.getSubject()} ${firstMsg.getPlainBody().substring(0, 800)}`;
      
      let labelsToApply = [];

      // Check against ALL rules (Poly-Hierarchy)
      RULES.forEach(rule => {
        if (rule.regex.test(content)) {
          labelsToApply = labelsToApply.concat(rule.labels);
        }
      });

      // Apply labels if matches found
      if (labelsToApply.length > 0) {
        // Remove duplicates
        labelsToApply = [...new Set(labelsToApply)]; 
        
        labelsToApply.forEach(labelName => {
          const label = GmailApp.getUserLabelByName(labelName);
          thread.addLabel(label);
        });
        
        Logger.log(`Processed: ${firstMsg.getSubject()} -> [${labelsToApply.join(", ")}]`);
        
        // OPTIONAL: Archive immediately if it hits a rule? 
        // Uncomment the next line to enable "Inbox Zero" automation
        // thread.moveToArchive();
      }
    });
  }
}

3. Why this approach is better for you

  1. Dual Tagging: If you buy a Raspberry Pi from Adafruit, the script detects "Adafruit" (Electronics) AND "Order Confirmed" (Receipts). It applies both 30_Projects/32_Electronics and 90_Finances/91_Receipts. You can find that email in either folder.
  2. Self-Healing: The ensureLabelsExist method means if you add a new rule in the code (e.g., 30_Projects/34_Woodworking), you don't have to go to Gmail settings to create the label. The script builds the infrastructure for you.
  3. Modular Regex: The RULES array is at the top. As you take on new contracts or new hobbies, you just add one line to the array.

4. The "Janitor" Script (Maintenance)

Since we are making this a larger project, we need a garbage collector. This script deletes "noise" that is useful today but trash tomorrow (like 2FA codes or shipping updates).

Add this function to your file:

function runJanitor() {
  const JANITOR_RULES = [
    { query: 'subject:"verification code" older_than:1d', action: "trash" },
    { query: 'subject:"shipping update" older_than:14d', action: "trash" },
    { query: 'label:10_Work/14_Job_Hunt older_than:30d', action: "archive" }, // Auto-archive old job alerts
    { query: 'category:promotions older_than:30d', action: "trash" }
  ];

  JANITOR_RULES.forEach(rule => {
    const threads = GmailApp.search(rule.query);
    if (threads.length > 0) {
      if (rule.action === "trash") {
        GmailApp.moveThreadsToTrash(threads);
      } else if (rule.action === "archive") {
        GmailApp.moveThreadsToArchive(threads);
      }
      Logger.log(`Janitor: ${rule.action}ed ${threads.length} threads matching ${rule.query}`);
    }
  });
}

Implementation Plan

  1. Deployment: Paste the code into your Apps Script project.
  2. Initial Run: Manually run runInboxProcessor. It might take a while to chew through your backlog. You can set up a "Time-Driven Trigger" to run it every 10 minutes.
  3. Janitor: Set a Time-Driven Trigger to run runJanitor once a day (e.g., at 2 AM).

This is the fun part. We are going to turn your email inbox into a read-only database and your Google Sheet into a live frontend.

Most people manually type expenses into Excel. We are going to automate that. When you buy a bee suit or a new sensor, the script will detect the receipt, tag it 90_Finances/91_Receipts, parse the dollar amount, and log it to a spreadsheet.

Phase 3: The Automated Ledger

Step 1: The Database (Google Sheet)

  1. Create a new Google Sheet.
  2. Name it "Life OS - Ledger 2026".
  3. Create a tab named Expenses_Raw.
  4. Add these headers in Row 1:
    • A1: Date
    • B1: Sender
    • C1: Subject
    • D1: Category (e.g., Electronics, Beekeeping)
    • E1: Estimated Amount
    • F1: Link (Direct URL to the email)

Copy the Spreadsheet ID from the URL (the long string between /d/ and /edit). You will need this for the code.

Step 2: The "FinanceLogger" Class

Add this new class to your script file. This module handles the "ETL" (Extract, Transform, Load) process. It uses regex to hunt for currency patterns ($12.99, USD 50.00) inside the email body.

class FinanceLogger {
  constructor(sheetId) {
    this.sheetId = sheetId;
    this.sheetName = "Expenses_Raw";
    this.currencyRegex = /\$\s?(\d{1,3}(?:,\d{3})*(?:\.\d{2})?)/; // Matches $10.99, $1,000.00
  }

  logTransaction(message, categoryTag) {
    const sheet = SpreadsheetApp.openById(this.sheetId).getSheetByName(this.sheetName);
    
    const date = message.getDate();
    const sender = message.getFrom();
    const subject = message.getSubject();
    const body = message.getPlainBody().substring(0, 2000); // Scan first 2k chars
    const threadId = message.getThread().getId();
    const link = `https://mail.google.com/mail/u/0/#inbox/${threadId}`;

    // 1. Attempt to find the dollar amount
    let amount = "0.00";
    const match = body.match(this.currencyRegex);
    if (match && match[1]) {
      amount = match[1].replace(/,/g, ''); // Remove commas for float conversion
    }

    // 2. Append to Sheet
    // We add ' ' to sender to prevent Excel injection issues, just in case.
    sheet.appendRow([date, sender, subject, categoryTag, amount, link]);
    
    Logger.log(`Logged finance item: ${subject} ($${amount})`);
  }
}

Step 3: Wiring it into the Main Processor

Now we need to update your main GmailProcessor class (from the previous turn) to utilize this new FinanceLogger.

I have updated the processInbox method below. Replace your old processInbox with this version.

Crucial: Replace YOUR_SHEET_ID_HERE with the ID you copied in Step 1.

// --- UPDATED CLASS DEFINITION ---
class GmailProcessor {
  constructor() {
    this.batchSize = 20; // Lower batch size since we are doing more heavy lifting now
    // REPLACE THIS WITH YOUR ACTUAL SHEET ID
    this.financeLogger = new FinanceLogger("YOUR_SHEET_ID_HERE"); 
  }

  ensureLabelsExist() {
    // (Same as before - keeps your folders created)
    const allLabels = new Set();
    RULES.forEach(r => r.labels.forEach(l => allLabels.add(l)));
    allLabels.forEach(l => { try { GmailApp.createLabel(l) } catch(e){} });
  }

  processInbox() {
    const threads = GmailApp.getInboxThreads(0, this.batchSize);
    
    threads.forEach(thread => {
      const messages = thread.getMessages();
      const firstMsg = messages[0];
      const content = `${firstMsg.getFrom()} ${firstMsg.getSubject()} ${firstMsg.getPlainBody().substring(0, 800)}`;
      
      let labelsToApply = [];
      let isFinance = false;
      let detectedCategory = "General";

      // Check against ALL rules
      RULES.forEach(rule => {
        if (rule.regex.test(content)) {
          labelsToApply = labelsToApply.concat(rule.labels);
          
          // Check if this rule is related to our Finance tags
          if (rule.labels.some(l => l.includes("90_Finances"))) {
            isFinance = true;
          }
          // Try to capture a specific category (e.g., Electronics) for the spreadsheet
          if (rule.labels.some(l => l.includes("30_Projects"))) {
            detectedCategory = rule.labels.find(l => l.includes("30_Projects")).split("/")[1];
          }
        }
      });

      // APPLY LABELS & LOG TO SHEET
      if (labelsToApply.length > 0) {
        labelsToApply = [...new Set(labelsToApply)];
        
        // 1. Apply Labels in Gmail
        labelsToApply.forEach(labelName => {
          const label = GmailApp.getUserLabelByName(labelName);
          thread.addLabel(label);
        });

        // 2. If it's a receipt, Log it to Sheets
        // We check if the thread already has the label to avoid double-logging
        const existingLabels = thread.getLabels().map(l => l.getName());
        const alreadyLogged = existingLabels.some(l => l.includes("90_Finances"));
        
        if (isFinance && !alreadyLogged) {
          this.financeLogger.logTransaction(firstMsg, detectedCategory);
        }
        
        // Optional: Archive
        // thread.moveToArchive();
      }
    });
  }
}

class Librarian {
  constructor() {
    // Map Gmail Labels to Drive Folder Names
    this.folderMap = {
      "90_Finances/91_Receipts": "Receipts",
      "90_Finances/93_Tax_Docs": "Contracts",
      "20_Academia/21_ISU_Masters": "School",
      "40_Logistics/41_Housing": "Contracts"
    };
    
    // Root folder ID (Replace with the ID from your 'LifeOS_Docs' URL)
    this.rootFolderId = "YOUR_DRIVE_FOLDER_ID_HERE"; 
  }

  run() {
    const rootFolder = DriveApp.getFolderById(this.rootFolderId);
    
    // Iterate through our configured labels
    for (const [labelName, subFolderName] of Object.entries(this.folderMap)) {
      this.processLabel(labelName, subFolderName, rootFolder);
    }
  }

  processLabel(labelName, subFolderName, rootFolder) {
    const label = GmailApp.getUserLabelByName(labelName);
    if (!label) return; // Skip if label doesn't exist yet

    // Get threads labeled in the last 24 hours to avoid scanning history forever
    // "older_than:0d" isn't valid, so we just grab the first X threads and check dates
    const threads = label.getThreads(0, 10); 

    threads.forEach(thread => {
      thread.getMessages().forEach(message => {
        // Only process if message is less than 1 day old
        if (new Date() - message.getDate() < 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000) { 
          const attachments = message.getAttachments();
          
          if (attachments.length > 0) {
            // Ensure subfolder exists
            const targetFolder = this.getOrCreateSubfolder(rootFolder, subFolderName);
            
            attachments.forEach(att => {
              // Rename: YYYY-MM-DD_Subject_Filename
              const datePrefix = Utilities.formatDate(message.getDate(), Session.getScriptTimeZone(), "yyyy-MM-dd");
              const cleanSubject = message.getSubject().replace(/[^a-zA-Z0-9]/g, "_").substring(0, 30);
              const newName = `${datePrefix}_${cleanSubject}_${att.getName()}`;
              
              // Check if file already exists to prevent duplicates
              const existing = targetFolder.getFilesByName(newName);
              if (!existing.hasNext()) {
                targetFolder.createFile(att).setName(newName);
                Logger.log(`Librarian saved: ${newName} to ${subFolderName}`);
              }
            });
          }
        }
      });
    });
  }

  getOrCreateSubfolder(parent, name) {
    const folders = parent.getFoldersByName(name);
    if (folders.hasNext()) return folders.next();
    return parent.createFolder(name);
  }
}

This module scans for high-priority keywords (like "Offer", "Lease", "Emergency"). When found, it can trigger a Webhook.

  • Use Case: You could have your Raspberry Pi flash an LED, or have Home Assistant turn your smart lights Red when a "Job Offer" comes in.

class Watcher {
  constructor() {
    this.criticalKeywords = /job offer|lease agreement|urgent|action required/i;
    // Optional: Replace with a Discord Webhook, IFTTT, or Ntfy.sh URL
    this.webhookUrl = ""; 
  }

  scanUrgent() {
    // Look strictly at Inbox (unprocessed)
    const threads = GmailApp.getInboxThreads(0, 20);
    
    threads.forEach(thread => {
      if (thread.isUnread()) {
        const subject = thread.getFirstMessageSubject();
        
        if (this.criticalKeywords.test(subject)) {
          Logger.log(`CRITICAL EMAIL FOUND: ${subject}`);
          
          // 1. Mark as Important in Gmail
          thread.markImportant();
          thread.addLabel(GmailApp.createLabel("00_Inbox_Triage/URGENT"));
          
          // 2. Fire Webhook (If configured)
          if (this.webhookUrl) {
            this.triggerWebhook(subject);
          }
        }
      }
    });
  }

  triggerWebhook(subject) {
    const payload = {
      content: `🚨 **PRIORITY ALERT** 🚨\nNew Critical Email: "${subject}"`
    };
    
    const options = {
      method: "post",
      contentType: "application/json",
      payload: JSON.stringify(payload)
    };
    
    try {
      UrlFetchApp.fetch(this.webhookUrl, options);
    } catch (e) {
      Logger.log("Webhook failed: " + e.toString());
    }
  }
}

Step 2: The "JobHunter" Class

class JobHunter {
  constructor(sheetId) {
    this.sheetId = sheetId;
    this.sheetName = "Job_Hunt_Funnel";
    
    // Heuristics for status determination
    this.statusPatterns = {
      "Offer": /offer letter|congratulations|pleased to offer/i,
      "Interview": /interview|phone screen|schedule a call|availability|code signal|hacker rank/i,
      "Rejection": /unfortunately|not moving forward|other candidates|careful consideration|pursue other/i,
      "Applied": /application received|thanks for applying|successfully submitted/i
    };
  }

  run() {
    // Look at the "10_Work/14_Job_Hunt" label we created earlier
    const label = GmailApp.getUserLabelByName("10_Work/14_Job_Hunt");
    if (!label) return;

    // Scan last 20 threads (assume we run this daily)
    const threads = label.getThreads(0, 20);

    threads.forEach(thread => {
      // Only process unread threads to avoid duplicates (or use a tracking ID system)
      // For this v1, we'll check if it's Unread, then mark Read.
      if (thread.isUnread()) {
        const message = thread.getMessages()[0];
        const subject = message.getSubject();
        const body = message.getPlainBody();
        const sender = message.getFrom();
        
        const status = this.determineStatus(subject, body);
        
        if (status) {
          const company = this.extractCompany(sender, subject, body);
          const position = this.extractPosition(subject, body);
          
          this.logApplication(new Date(), company, status, position, thread.getPermalink());
          
          // Optional: Mark read so we don't double-log
          // thread.markRead(); 
        }
      }
    });
  }

  determineStatus(subject, body) {
    const text = subject + " " + body.substring(0, 500); // Check first 500 chars
    if (this.statusPatterns["Offer"].test(text)) return "OFFER 🚨";
    if (this.statusPatterns["Rejection"].test(text)) return "Rejected";
    if (this.statusPatterns["Interview"].test(text)) return "Interview";
    if (this.statusPatterns["Applied"].test(text)) return "Applied";
    return null; // No clear status found
  }

  extractCompany(sender, subject, body) {
    // 1. Try to get it from the sender name (e.g., "Google Careers" -> "Google")
    let company = sender.split('<')[0].replace(/careers|jobs|team|recruiting/gi, "").trim();
    
    // 2. Fallback: If sender is generic (like "no-reply@greenhouse.io"), try to find "at [Company]"
    if (company.includes("no-reply") || company.length < 2) {
      const match = body.match(/at ([A-Z][a-z]+(?: [A-Z][a-z]+)*)/);
      if (match) company = match[1];
    }
    return company.replace(/"/g, "");
  }

  extractPosition(subject, body) {
    // Simple extraction for common titles
    const match = body.match(/(software engineer|developer|manager|teacher)/i);
    return match ? match[0] : "Unknown Role";
  }

  logApplication(date, company, status, position, link) {
    const sheet = SpreadsheetApp.openById(this.sheetId).getSheetByName(this.sheetName);
    sheet.appendRow([date, company, status, position, link]);
    Logger.log(`Job Hunter: Logged ${status} for ${company}`);
  }
}

Module 9: The Warranty Vault (Calendar Integration)

This script scans your receipts. If it sees a purchase over $100 (configurable), it automatically calculates a 1-year expiration date and puts a "Warranty Expiring" event on your Google Calendar.

Step 1: Enable Calendar API (Just like you did for Tasks, ensure the "Calendar" service is added in the left sidebar).

Step 2: Add this Class

class WarrantyVault {
  constructor() {
    this.calendarName = "LifeOS_Warranties"; // We will create a specific calendar for this
    this.minThreshold = 100.00; // Only track items costing more than this
    this.defaultWarrantyDays = 365;
  }

  run() {
    // 1. Get or Create the Calendar
    let calendar = CalendarApp.getCalendarsByName(this.calendarName)[0];
    if (!calendar) {
      calendar = CalendarApp.createCalendar(this.calendarName);
      Logger.log(`Created new calendar: ${this.calendarName}`);
    }

    // 2. Scan Receipts (Reuse the Finance/Receipts label)
    const label = GmailApp.getUserLabelByName("90_Finances/91_Receipts");
    if (!label) return;

    // We use PropertiesService to remember which emails we've already processed
    // This prevents creating duplicate calendar events every time the script runs.
    const scriptProperties = PropertiesService.getScriptProperties();

    const threads = label.getThreads(0, 20); // Check last 20 receipts

    threads.forEach(thread => {
      const msg = thread.getMessages()[0];
      const msgId = msg.getId();

      // Skip if already processed
      if (scriptProperties.getProperty(msgId)) return;

      const body = msg.getPlainBody();
      const subject = msg.getSubject();
      
      // Extract Price
      const priceMatch = body.match(/\$\s?(\d{1,3}(?:,\d{3})*(?:\.\d{2})?)/);
      if (priceMatch) {
        const price = parseFloat(priceMatch[1].replace(/,/g, ''));
        
        if (price >= this.minThreshold) {
          // Calculate Expiration
          const purchaseDate = msg.getDate();
          const expiryDate = new Date(purchaseDate);
          expiryDate.setDate(purchaseDate.getDate() + this.defaultWarrantyDays);

          // Create Calendar Event
          const eventTitle = `⚠️ Warranty Expiring: ${subject.substring(0, 30)}...`;
          const description = `Original Price: $${price}\nLink: ${thread.getPermalink()}\n\nFull Item Details inside email.`;
          
          calendar.createAllDayEvent(eventTitle, expiryDate, {description: description});
          
          Logger.log(`Warranty Vault: Tracked item "${subject}" ($${price})`);
        }
      }
      
      // Mark as processed regardless of price, so we don't scan it again
      scriptProperties.setProperty(msgId, "true");
    });
  }
}

class DailyBriefing {

    expenseData.forEach(row => {

      const rowDate = Utilities.formatDate(new Date(row[0]), Session.getScriptTimeZone(), "yyyy-MM-dd");

      let isExpense = false;
      let category = "General";

      RULES.forEach(rule => {
        if (rule.regex.test(content)) {
          labelsToAdd = labelsToAdd.concat(rule.labels);
          if (rule.labels.some(l => l.includes("90_Finances"))) isExpense = true;
          if (rule.labels.some(l => l.includes("30_Projects"))) category = rule.labels[0].split("/")[1];
        }
      });

      if (labelsToAdd.length > 0) {
        // Apply Tags
        [...new Set(labelsToAdd)].forEach(l => thread.addLabel(GmailApp.getUserLabelByName(l)));
        
        // Log Expense
        if (isExpense && !this.isDuplicate(thread)) {
          this.logExpense(msg, category);
        }
      }
    });
  }

  ensureLabels() {
    const allLabels = new Set();
    RULES.forEach(r => r.labels.forEach(l => allLabels.add(l)));
    allLabels.forEach(l => { try { GmailApp.createLabel(l) } catch(e){} });
  }

  isDuplicate(thread) {
    // Simple check: does it already have the label?
    return thread.getLabels().some(l => l.getName().includes("90_Finances"));
  }

  logExpense(msg, category) {
    const amount = (msg.getPlainBody().match(/\$\s?(\d{1,3}(?:,\d{3})*(?:\.\d{2})?)/) || [])[1];
    if (amount) {
      this.sheet.appendRow([new Date(), msg.getFrom(), msg.getSubject(), category, amount.replace(/,/g,''), `https://mail.google.com/mail/u/0/#inbox/${msg.getThread().getId()}`]);
    }
  }
}

// --- MODULE 2: THE JOB HUNTER (Career CRM) ---
class JobHunter {
  run() {
    const label = GmailApp.getUserLabelByName("10_Work/14_Job_Hunt");
    if (!label) return;
    const sheet = SpreadsheetApp.openById(CONFIG.SHEET_ID).getSheetByName("Job_Hunt");
    
    label.getThreads(0, 10).forEach(thread => {
      if (thread.isUnread()) {
        const msg = thread.getMessages()[0];
        const status = this.analyze(msg.getSubject() + " " + msg.getPlainBody());
        
        if (status) {
          const company = msg.getFrom().split('<')[0].replace(/"/g, "").trim();
          sheet.appendRow([new Date(), company, status, "Software Engineer", thread.getPermalink()]);
          // thread.markRead(); // Optional
        }
      }
    });
  }

  analyze(text) {
    if (/offer letter|congratulations/i.test(text)) return "OFFER";
    if (/interview|availability/i.test(text)) return "Interview";
    if (/unfortunately|not moving forward/i.test(text)) return "Rejected";
    if (/received|successfully submitted/i.test(text)) return "Applied";
    return null;
  }
}

// --- MODULE 3: THE LIBRARIAN (File Backup) ---
class Librarian {
  run() {
    const map = {
      "90_Finances/91_Receipts": "Receipts",
      "90_Finances/93_Tax_Docs": "Contracts",
      "20_Academia/21_ISU": "School"
    };
    const root = DriveApp.getFolderById(CONFIG.DRIVE_ROOT_ID);
    
    for (const [labelName, folderName] of Object.entries(map)) {
      const label = GmailApp.getUserLabelByName(labelName);
      if (!label) continue;
      
      label.getThreads(0, 5).forEach(t => {
        t.getMessages().forEach(m => {
          if ((new Date() - m.getDate()) < 24*60*60*1000) { // Only last 24h
            m.getAttachments().forEach(att => {
              const target = this.getSubfolder(root, folderName);
              const name = `${Utilities.formatDate(m.getDate(), Session.getScriptTimeZone(), "yyyy-MM-dd")}_${att.getName()}`;
              if (!target.getFilesByName(name).hasNext()) target.createFile(att).setName(name);
            });
          }
        });
      });
    }
  }

  getSubfolder(parent, name) {
    const iter = parent.getFoldersByName(name);
    return iter.hasNext() ? iter.next() : parent.createFolder(name);
  }
}

// --- MODULE 6: WARRANTY VAULT ---
class WarrantyVault {
  run() {
    const label = GmailApp.getUserLabelByName("90_Finances/91_Receipts");
    if (!label) return;
    const props = PropertiesService.getScriptProperties();
    
    label.getThreads(0, 10).forEach(t => {
      const msg = t.getMessages()[0];
      if (props.getProperty(msg.getId())) return;
      
      const price = (msg.getPlainBody().match(/\$\s?(\d+)/) || [])[1];
      if (price && parseFloat(price) > CONFIG.WARRANTY_THRESHOLD) {
         const cal = CalendarApp.getDefaultCalendar(); // Or specific ID
         const date = new Date();
         date.setDate(date.getDate() + 365);
         cal.createAllDayEvent(`⚠️ Warranty Expires: ${t.getFirstMessageSubject()}`, date);
      }
      props.setProperty(msg.getId(), "true");
    });
  }
}

5. Final Setup Instructions (The "Restart")

  1. Apps Script Settings:
    • Enable Tasks API and Calendar API under "Services" on the left sidebar.
    • Paste your Sheet ID and Drive Folder ID into Config.gs.
  2. Initialize:
    • Run runLifeOS manually once. It will create all 15 labels in your Gmail automatically.
    • It may ask for permissions (Gmail, Drive, Sheets, Tasks, Calendar). Approve them.
  3. Automate:
    • Go to Triggers (Clock icon).
    • Create Trigger 1: runLifeOS -> Time-driven -> Every 15 Minutes.
    • Create Trigger 2: runMorningReport -> Time-driven -> Day Timer -> 6am to 7am.
